Alex  great speaking earlier, thanks for the context. Quick post-call recap and concrete next steps below. I attached the initial eval CSV and prompt sets we discussed.

Recap (short):
- Goal: high-precision product Q&A with low hallucination.
- Data: 12M docs (product + support); Pinecone vector store.
- Latency target: <600ms tail for user chats.

Recommended starting config (we recommend iterating from here):
- Chunking:  Chunk size 150 tokens, overlap 50 tokens (helps long doc handling).
- Retrieval: top_k = 50 (candidate pool), filter by metadata doc_type and product_version when applicable.
- Embeddings: use redwood-embedding-1 for indexing / similarity (balanced cost/quality).
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for final re-ranking (rerank_top_k = 10)  improves precision@1 at cost of extra latency; use only when user-facing path requires highest precision.
- Generator model: prefer Redwood-Instruct-13B for production (good cost/quality tradeoff); fallback to Llama-2-70B-chat for very difficult queries where more knowledge is needed.
- Caching: enable prefix caching for repeated help topics, TTL 12h for popular Qs.

Metrics / evals to track: precision@1, recall@5, grounded_answer_rate (fraction of answers with >=1 supporting doc), hallucination_rate (manual eval), mean latency (p50/p95), cost per 1k queries.

Attachments: acme_rag_eval_results.csv (baseline retrieval/rerank numbers), prompt_sets_v2.zip (QA prompt + stress cases).

Next steps:
1) We'll share a runnable eval script and a Benchmark Drive folder (link below).
2) Logan / Dylan will propose a low-latency reranker path (cross-encoder on dedicated pool vs. two-stage lightweight reranker).
3) Schedule a 30-min sync next week to review results after you run baseline.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeRagEval (prompt sets + eval harness), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/rag-grounding-2026

Adding engineering specifics from our infra perspective  quick suggestions you can try in your lab: 

1) Retriever indexing: use 150-token chunks, store chunk-level metadata (doc_id, source, product_version). Use HNSW index in Pinecone with ef_search=128 for recall.

2) Embeddings: redwood-embedding-1 (index with float32, optionally quantize to int8 if you need storage savings).

3) Candidate selection vs final rerank:
   - Stage 1 (fast): ANN retrieval top_k=50, simple lexical BM25 filter for exact name matches (helps product code lookups).
   - Stage 2 (slow/high-precision): cross-encoder reranker (we tested MiniLM-cross-2.1 cross-encoder trained on in-domain pairs) rerank_top_k=10. Expect +8-12% lift in precision@1 vs no reranker on our baseline.

4) Latency considerations: run cross-encoder on a small dedicated pool (1-2 gpus) and only call when p95 latency budget allows. For strict latency path, consider a learned lightweight reranker (bi-encoder scoring) as a compromise: ~+4-6% precision@1 improvement with 1/3 the cost of cross-encoder.

5) Grounding signals: for each candidate compute overlap_score (token overlap with source), citation_score (presence of explicit product identifiers), and model_confidence. Use a simple rule: require citation_score > 0 for auto-responses; otherwise route to triage.

I attached a quick CSV with our baseline numbers (acme_rag_eval_results.csv). Happy to run a short POC on a sample export if ACME can share ~10k docs.

 Logan
Logan Wright

Thanks  this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 
1) When you say rerank_top_k=10, is that after top_k=50 retrieval?
2) For the grounding rule (citation_score > 0), what do you recommend as the threshold for citation_score in your tooling?
3) We're willing to share a 10k doc export for POC  what's the easiest secure method?

Also, we saw the baseline CSV  precision@1 of 0.62 without reranker and 0.71 with cross-encoder is promising. Can you confirm the eval prompt set you used (we want to reproduce exactly)?

Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Alex  short answers inline and action items below.

1) Yes: rerank_top_k=10 is applied after you retrieve top_k=50 candidates. We recommend keeping top_k >= 50 to ensure recall for long-tail Qs.

2) Citation score: our current heuristic scales 0-1. For ACME's product docs I suggest threshold >= 0.25 (i.e., at least some token overlap on key identifiers). We also recommend a small human-verified seed set to tune this threshold against your tolerance for false-positives.

3) Secure POC transfer: preferred is a short-lived GCS bucket or S3 presigned URL. If you need we can provide a dedicated intake link and MSA addendum  Priya, please coordinate with ACME on the procurement side.

Eval prompt set: the prompt_sets_v2.zip in the Drive folder is the exact set used for the baseline numbers (QA canonical + adversarial stress cases). We included an eval README with the harness and seeds so you can reproduce.

Action items:
- ACME: share 10k doc export to our S3 intake (we'll send presigned link after signing NDA/PO as needed).
- Redwood: Logan + Neha will prepare a reproducible eval script and a lightweight reranker variant to test (ETA by Thu 4/16).
- Schedule: I'll set a 30-min sync for the week of 4/20 to review first POC results.

If that's all aligned I'll send the presigned link + short intake instructions.

Thanks  Marissa
